summary: Lighthouse on the southwest tip of Molokai, established 2 January 1882; Burrows family keepers, automated in 1912, a skeleton tower and a pole light since.

lens.note: Fixed white fourth-order Fresnel light at the 1882 opening (LighthouseFriends, quoting the Notice to Mariners). The 1912 apparatus was a 375 mm lens lantern (Light Station Report).

access.note: Site open, tower closed (Lighthouse Directory). The 1912 report says the point can be landed on in calm weather; the shore is rough and volcanic.

corrections.why: The station was established and the light first exhibited on 2 January 1882 (1912 Light Station Report: 'First Built or Established: January 2, 1882'; LighthouseFriends). 1912 is the year of the automation and the new iron tower, which the Directory's 'station established 1912' appears to record.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The record's conflict note says LighthouseFriends was recorded as 'lost' while OpenStreetMap maps a standing structure. LighthouseFriends describes a flashing white light on a pole near the point (2022) and the Directory describes an active light; the story gives those. The USLHS place record (source 5) gives 'Existing: No' and 'Active Aid to Navigation?: No'. The story reports that as a disagreement and does not use it to date anything.
The 1912 report gives 2 January 1882 as the date the station was first built or established. The Directory's 'station established 1912' matches the 1912 rebuild and automation.

The 1882 light was fifty feet above the sea (Notice to Mariners, via LighthouseFriends; the USLHS place record also gives 50 ft). From 1912 the focal plane was 151 ft (46 m), as in the record and the Directory.

notes_for_editor: (1) Coast Guard Historian page not used. The Coast Guard Historian's article for this light (Lae o Ha La'au Point Light, archived copy at web.archive.org/web/20231208055126id_/...) has the right facts (established 2 Jan 1882; automated 1912; 20 ft cast-iron then steel pole; solar light 1972; keepers J.W. Burrows 1882-1898 and J.R. Burrows 1898-1912). The article sits inside a form element, which fetch_text's text reducer drops, so check_quotes cannot verify any quote from it. Fix the reducer or cite it when it can be read. (2) Ship name: LighthouseFriends says H. V. Carleton; the Coast Guard timeline says H.N. Carleton. (3) Tower after 1912: the 1912 report says an iron skeleton tower; LighthouseFriends says a wood trestle tower on the bluff. The story states both and says which is the report's; the disagreement is not resolved. The Directory's 35 ft tower (a Coast Guard photo) is the 1906 wooden tower. (4) The USLHS place record gives 'original lens year 1889'; no source read confirms it, so it is not used. (5) John W. Burrows: roster 1881-1898; LighthouseFriends has him at work in December 1881. (6) E. H.N. Kanahele: the roster says laborer; LighthouseFriends lists him among the keepers. The record follows the roster. (7) Checked 2026-10-28 against the page image (PDF p. 37, printed p. 37): the list reads 'Barbers Point, Oahu; Laau' at the foot of one column and 'Point, Molokai; Makena Point, Maui; and Mahukona, Hawaii' at the top of the next, so La'au is named among the lights established prior to 1890. (8) The 1937 Bulletin's two-flash occulting pattern is not the current 2.5 s flash; no source read dates that change. (9) Range: the record's 7 nm (NOAA ENC) is not used; the 1882 notice claimed eleven miles. (10) Same-name risk: the Directory's Molokai (Kalaupapa) light of 1909 and the Commissioner's 'Molokai Light Station' are the north-coast Kalaupapa light, not La'au. (11) The 1912 and 1937 Bulletins' OCR splits words ('L ae 0 Ka L aa u', 'DBKE-200' reads cleanly; the 1937 heading is split across columns, so only 'IMPROVEMENT OF UNWATCHED' is quoted). (12) No access road or boat route for the point today is in the sources read; the Directory says only 'site open, tower closed'. (13) Checked 2026-10-28: the 1912 Bulletin (PDF p. 26) lists 'Lae o Ka Laau Point, Molokai Island, Hawaii (acetylene)' under 'Lights changed from fixed to flashing or occulting'. The 1937 Bulletin (PDF p. 6) gives the Dalen LBUA and DBKE-200 installation at Laau Point and an intensity 'from 390 to approximately 1,640 English candles'. The 1882 Notice to Mariners is known only as LighthouseFriends prints it, and the story attributes it so. The 1912 report's 'Site: Purchase' supports the 'bought' wording. The place record's 1889 lens date is not used.
